newsitem.title: USA: Morris CEO open to tobacco-disputes measures.
newsitem.headline: Morris CEO open to tobacco-disputes measures.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc chief executive Geoffrey Bible said on Thursday that the beleaguered but highly profitable tobacco giant was open to "reasonable measures" aimed at resolving mushrooming anti-tobacco lawsuits and other smoking disputes in the United States.

Declining to comment directly on secret talks between cigarette companies and anti-tobacco forces on a possible sweeping resolution of many of the lawsuits and regulatory questions, Bible told shareholders at the company's annual meeting, "We will listen and explore all reasonable measures ...".
But he also said Philip Morris, the target of hundreds of individual, state-government and class-action suits in the United States, would continue fighting the lawsuits "vigorously."

Bible said Philip Morris was willing to work with government officials and others on hammering out new regulation of tobacco sales, even as industry now fights in court Food and Drug Administration rules on tobacco sales put in place this year.
"We are willing to work with responsible government representatives and others on a balanced system," Bible said.

The executive did not spell out particular initiatives he might consider, other than to say Philip Morris favored restrictions on young people buying cigarettes and had in 1995 launched its own program to limit people under 21 from obtaining cigarettes.
"We do not want kids to smoke," Bible said.
